elements.description: Integrates the input with forward Euler: y[n+1] = y[n] + dt*x[n]. Publishes initial_value first and stages the next state for the following step; can close feedback loops. Oscillator amplitude can grow with this method; timestep refinement is needed for accuracy.

parameters.description: Pins the element's type (otherwise inferred from connections)

parameters.description: Positive finite model timestep in seconds, using the signal's real component type. Must agree with the graph rate; Studio Run Configuration sets it.

elements.description: Integrates the input with the trapezoidal rule. Default implicit mode solves coupled endpoint states together and supplies causal memory. Its bounded fixed-point solve reports nonconvergence; reduce dt if it fails. Sampled mode instead integrates supplied samples with direct feedthrough.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Pins the element's type (otherwise inferred from connections)

parameters.name: dt
parameters.description: Positive finite model timestep in seconds, using the signal's real component type. Must agree with the graph rate; smaller steps can improve implicit convergence.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: implicit: y[n+1]=y[n]+dt/2*(f[n]+f[n+1]), with jointly solved feedback states; only supported side-effect-free trial dependencies may vary with the endpoint. sampled: y[n]=y[n-1]+dt/2*(input[n-1]+input[n]); first call records input and leaves initial_value unchanged. Sampled mode cannot alone close a feedback loop.

elements.description: Semi-implicit Euler for x'' = acceleration: v[n+1] = v[n] + dt*a[n], x[n+1] = x[n] + dt*v[n+1]; causal memory publishes position/velocity together on the following step. First-order accurate; for a position-dependent conservative harmonic oscillator, energy error is bounded within the method's stable timestep range, not exactly conserved. Velocity-dependent acceleration loses the symplectic property.

input_ports.name: acceleration
input_ports.description: Acceleration/force input, a(x) computed by the surrounding graph; a velocity dependency (damping) loses the symplectic energy bound.
